answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the pearl identifier and voids the later submissions, as a result the operator pays for 161 runs and collects one. Because the river index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the kernel audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 161 answers need 161 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
